summary: Crop Rotation Crash Test is a web tool that stress-tests a farmer’s planting plan against 45 years of real NASA POWER weather (1981–2025). For every year it estimates crop water stress, yield and profit (FAO-56/FAO-33 methods), shows which years the plan would have lost money, and searches thousands of rotations for a more resilient or water-saving plan. Demo fields: Kostanay, Akmola and Kyzylorda (irrigated rice in the Syr Darya/Aral Sea basin).
details: The user picks a field and a crop sequence. The tool downloads NASA POWER daily temperature and precipitation, computes reference evapotranspiration (Hargreaves, FAO-56), runs a soil water balance with crop coefficients, estimates yield loss from water stress (FAO-33 Ky) and rotation effects (legumes, fallow, crop breaks), then profit. An optimizer compares all 2–4 year rotations by profit, loss years or water use. Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet and OpenStreetMap. Prices and costs are editable examples; the model compares plans and is not an exact yield forecast.
